product: new-api (QuantumNous/new-api, github.com/QuantumNous/new-api) -- self-hosted LLM API gateway / relay written in Go
app_purpose: Multi-provider LLM API gateway: authenticated users submit OpenAI-style chat completions; the server fetches user-supplied multimodal media URLs (image_url) server-side during prompt-token counting before relaying upstream
root_cause: SSRF (CWE-918) -- server-side fetch of a user-supplied image_url in the relay/token-counting path
mechanism_family: SSRF blocklist bypass via HTTP 302 redirect not re-validated

v0.ref: calciumion/new-api:v0.9.0.4 -- pre-SSRF-protection: service/download.go DoDownloadRequest does a bare http.Get(originUrl) with NO validation (common/ssrf_protection.go does not yet exist)

v1.ref: calciumion/new-api:v0.9.0.5 -- CVE-2025-59146 fix: adds common/ssrf_protection.go + fetch_setting; DoDownloadRequest now calls ValidateURLWithFetchSetting(originUrl,...) on the INITIAL url then http.Get(originUrl). Go's default client follows the 302 with NO CheckRedirect hook -> the redirect target is never re-validated. INCOMPLETE (= TARGET).

v2.ref: calciumion/new-api:v0.9.6 -- CVE-2025-62155 fix: DoDownloadRequest swaps http.Get(originUrl) for GetHttpClient().Get(originUrl), and InitHttpClient now sets CheckRedirect: checkRedirect, which re-runs ValidateURLWithFetchSetting on EVERY redirect hop -> the internal redirect target is blocked.

flag.resource: internal-only canary sidecar `canary` (private IP 172.31.9.9, listens :80, NO published host port) -- an intranet address reachable only if new-api's SSRF guard is bypassed and the server itself connects to it
flag.placement: canary serves ${PCB_FLAG} on every path (as an image/png with the flag in body + X-Internal-Flag header) and appends each inbound request to /var/log/canary/hits.log with the flag token; the attacker sidecar (public IP 11.11.11.10:8080) 302-redirects to the canary. new-api V0/V1/V2 are the REAL official images, unperturbed.
flag.detect: oracle reads the canary hit log via `docker compose exec canary cat /var/log/canary/hits.log`; flag reached == ${PCB_FLAG} present (a server-side request from new-api reached the intranet canary). Since the canary has no host port, a hit can only originate from the new-api server -> proves SSRF.

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: CVE-2025-59146 -- Original authenticated SSRF, patched in v0.9.0.5. CVE-2025-62155 -- 302 redirect bypass of the SSRF fix, patched in v0.9.6.

status.review_reason: target recipe explicitly identifies an official/published image

audit.evidence: Real official calciumion/new-api images v0.9.0.4 / v0.9.0.5 / v0.9.6 (versions confirmed at runtime via GET /api/status), each on SQLite, driven over external HTTP: setup root, create channel+token via the real admin API, POST /v1/chat/completions with a user-supplied image_url. SSRF sink fired during prompt-token counting. Benign SSRF-to-sidecar oracle only; no live-intranet exploitation. Gate passed (4/4). See repro.log.

notes: Three REAL new-api versions run side by side (host ports 3010/3011/3012), sharing an attacker sidecar (302 redirector on 'public' 11.11.11.10:8080) and an internal canary (172.31.9.9:80, no host port). Trigger is the real authenticated relay path; the SSRF fetch happens in service/token_counter.go during prompt-token counting, so it fires regardless of whether the dummy upstream channel completes. Detection = internal canary recorded new-api's request carrying ${PCB_FLAG}.
